title: Execution of the verdict tail
statement: Let $W$ be a word width, let $P$ be a program, and let $p$ be a program position such that the tail code for a Boolean decision $d$ at position $p$ occurs in $P$ starting at $p$. Suppose a memory $m$ stores the word representing an integer $r$ at the stack location of the main frame and the word representing $0$ at the zero location, and suppose $-2^W \le -2r < 2^W$. Then execution from position $p$ with memory $m$ reaches, in at most three steps, a configuration whose execution terminates with the verdict that is true exactly when $d$ is false or $r$ is positive; its result location stores the word representing $r$, and its memory agrees with $m$ outside the result and decision locations.
hypotheses_covered: The tail code for decision d at position p occurs in program P starting at p
The stack location of the main frame in m stores the word representing r
The zero location in m stores the word representing 0
The execution takes at most three steps
